```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE, fig.align = "center",
  fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4.2, dpi = 150,
  message = FALSE, warning = FALSE
)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(targets); library(dplyr); library(ggplot2) })
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 15))

# Every number in this deck is read from the {targets} store of rjkdc-analysis/;
# nothing is retyped except the paper's printed values we compare against.
store <- "../../_targets"
tr <- function(name) tar_read_raw(name, store = store)
for (f in list.files("../../R", pattern = "\\.R$", full.names = TRUE)) source(f)
rc <- tr("revenue_chain"); pf <- tr("pareto_fit"); t8 <- tr("income_tax_table8")
mcn <- tr("npv_mc_nber")
nc <- tr("nber_ceiling"); ncol <- tr("nber_collectible"); hl <- tr("site_headlines")
outputs <- read.csv("../../export/r/outputs.csv"); inputs <- read.csv("../../export/r/inputs.csv")
nb <- formals(compute_npv_mc_nber)
num <- function(x, d = 1) { s <- formatC(abs(x), format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ","); ifelse(x < 0, paste0("&minus;", s), s) }
usdb <- function(x, d = 1) paste0(ifelse(x < 0, "−$", "$"), formatC(abs(x), format = "f", digits = d), "B")
h <- function(v, q, col = "reproduced") hl[[col]][hl$version == v & hl$quantity == q]
out <- function(id, col = "value") outputs[[col]][outputs$output_id == id]
inp <- function(id) inputs$value[inputs$input_id == id]
dials <- site_dials(rc)
mm_lines <- sub("^## ", "", grep("^## [0-9]+\\.", readLines("../../MISMATCHES.md"), value = TRUE))
mm_first <- grepl("^[0-9]+\\. First version: ", mm_lines)
# The break-even table at the paper's central revenue (q x 72) and midpoint income tax
n10 <- compute_npv_table10(scenarios = list(central = list(label = "Central", WT = 0.5 * nb$wt_max, C = 4.55)))
eps7 <- 100 * (1 - nc$ceiling_recomputed / nc$domestic_total_grown) / (100 * inp("tax_rate"))
lit_loss <- 1 - (1 - inp("tax_rate"))^inp("brulhart_semi_elasticity")
# ties to the pipeline: a drift fails the render instead of shipping
stopifnot(round(ncol$central, 1) == h("nber", "revenue_headline", "printed"),
          round(mcn$summary$mean, 1) == h("nber", "mc_mean_npv", "printed"),
          abs(ncol$central - ncol$q * ncol$recognized) < 1e-9)
```

name: part-claim
class: center, middle, inverse

# Part 1: The claim

---

# What is being estimated

**Proposition 40** taxes, once, 5% of the net worth of billionaires who lived in California on
1 January 2026 (payable over five years). The [BSZ report](../../../bsz-analysis/site/) estimates it at about $100 billion.

The JR analysis asks a different question: **is the state better off, counting what it loses?**

$$NPV = WT - f \cdot \frac{C}{r}$$

.pull-left[

- $WT$: wealth tax collected, **once**
- $C$: income tax the billionaires pay, **per year**
- $f$: share of that income tax that leaves the state
- $r$: discount rate; $C/r$ is a stream of $C$ **for ever**, valued today

]

.pull-right[

.highlight-box[
The whole argument is a race between a one-time sum and a perpetuity. At $r$ = 1.5%, losing
one dollar a year for ever costs as much as losing `r num(1/0.015, 0)` dollars today.
]

]

---
name: headline

# The headline

**NBER chapter c15504** (Tax Policy and the Economy, vol. 41), 22 September 2026: Jaros and Rauh, litigation-weighted (the first
version, March 2026, was by Rauh, Jaros, Kearney, Doran and Cosso)

.big[`r usdb(h("nber","mc_mean_npv","printed"))`]
mean NPV; `r h("nber","mc_pct_negative","printed")`% of outcomes negative (PDF p.35, Figure 3 note; 85% in the text, p.1)<sup>1</sup><br>
revenue "approximately 30 billion" (`r usdb(h("nber","revenue_range_low","printed"))` to `r usdb(h("nber","revenue_range_high","printed"))`)

Reproduced: `r num(mcn$summary$mean, 2)` (the authors' seeded run, replayed draw for draw) and
`r num(tr("npv_mc_nber_analytic_mean"), 2)` (the exact expectation of the same draws).

.blue-box[
This is the **main estimate** of this Open Policy Analysis. The rest of the deck builds it:
the revenue (Part 2), the income tax (Part 3), the perpetuity (Part 4) and the Monte Carlo
that averages them (Part 5).
]

.footnote[<sup>1</sup> The authors' first version (Rauh, Jaros, Kearney, Doran and Cosso, Hoover Institution, SSRN 6340778, March 2026) printed `r usdb(h("ssrn","mc_mean_npv","printed"))` with `r h("ssrn","mc_pct_negative","printed")`% negative. The pipeline reproduces it too; see the appendix of [the report](../repro.html#appendix-first-version).]

---
name: part-revenue
class: center, middle, inverse

# Part 2: The revenue

---
name: revenue

# From $94 billion to about $30 billion (Sec 4)

```{r revchain, fig.height=3.4}
d <- data.frame(
  step = c("No one leaves\n(4.1)", "Grown 7% to the\nvaluation date (4.1)", "7 publicly reported\nmoves (4.3)",
           "Pre-filing leavers and\nZuckerberg out (4.4)", "Times q = 0.50\n(4.4)"),
  v = c(rc$baseline_precise, nc$domestic_total_grown, nc$ceiling_recomputed, ncol$recognized, ncol$central))
d$step <- factor(d$step, levels = d$step)
ggplot(d, aes(step, v)) + geom_col(fill = c(rep("#9a9a9a", 4), "#1f6b3b"), width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", v)), vjust = -0.4, size = 5) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "$B") + ylim(0, 112)
```

.small[
Each step sums 5% of each stayer's net worth, minus their home. The first four bars come out of the
authors' workbook and person-level file. The last multiplies by $q$ = `r num(ncol$q, 2)`, the chance the
Act survives in court, borrowed from an accounting rule (ASC 740-10): a judgement, not an estimate.
Printed: $`r h("nber","revenue_headline","printed")` billion, range $`r h("nber","revenue_range_low","printed")` to $`r h("nber","revenue_range_high","printed")` billion (PDF p.23).
]

---

# The semi-elasticity: a 5-point tax, how much base leaves?

$$\varepsilon = \frac{\%\Delta\,\text{base}}{\Delta\,\text{rate (points)}}$$

.pull-left[

- **Observed, 7 departures:** the grown base falls `r num(100*(1 - nc$ceiling_recomputed/nc$domestic_total_grown), 1)`%,
  so $\varepsilon$ = `r num(eps7, 2)` (printed 5.73, PDF p.22), a floor
- **Swiss literature** (Brülhart et al. 2022): 0.24 × 43 = `r inp("brulhart_semi_elasticity")`;
  in log form, `r num(100*lit_loss, 1)`% of the base leaves (PDF p.24)

]

.pull-right[

.highlight-box[
Two things to argue with: the Swiss estimate comes from a **recurring** tax, applied here to a
**one-time** one (the authors argue taxpayers treat it as the start of a recurring one); and this
check does not enter the Monte Carlo, which draws revenue from 0 to 72.
]

]

---
name: part-income
class: center, middle, inverse

# Part 3: The income tax

---
name: income-tax-c

# How much do billionaires pay each year? (Sec 5.1)

.pull-left[

**Upper bound.** Fit a Pareto tail to the Franchise Tax Board's (FTB, the state tax agency) filer counts above 1M to 10M dollars of income:
$\hat\alpha$ = `r num(pf$alpha, 2)`. If the 212 billionaires *are* the 212 highest earners, they pay
**$`r num(t8$mean_fy25[t8$K == 212], 2)` billion** a year.

**But** wealth is not income: many billionaires realise little in a given year. So place them at random
among the top $K$ filers (Table 9).

]

.pull-right[

```{r table8, fig.width=5.6, fig.height=3.6}
ggplot(t8, aes(K, mean_fy25)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05_fy25, ymax = p95_fy25), fill = "#1f6b3b", alpha = 0.18) +
  geom_line(colour = "#1f6b3b", linewidth = 1) + geom_point(colour = "#1f6b3b") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 500, linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = "pool size K", y = "$B per year") + theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

]

.highlight-box[
The authors call $K \approx 500$ "a reasonable lower bound": `r usdb(t8$mean_fy25[t8$K == 500], 2)`.
So $C \in [3.3, 5.8]$: a range between a model's upper bound and a **judgement** about the floor.
]

---
name: part-forever
class: center, middle, inverse

# Part 4: For ever

---
name: perpetuity

# The perpetuity multiplier (Sec 5.2)

```{r mult, fig.height=3.2}
r <- seq(0.01, 0.06, by = 0.0005)
ggplot(data.frame(r, m = 1 / r), aes(100 * r, m)) + geom_line(linewidth = 1, colour = "#1f6b3b") +
  annotate("point", x = c(1.5, 3, 4.5), y = 1 / c(0.015, 0.03, 0.045), size = 3) +
  annotate("text", x = c(1.5, 3, 4.5), y = 1 / c(0.015, 0.03, 0.045) + 9,
           label = sprintf("%.0f", 1 / c(0.015, 0.03, 0.045)), size = 5) +
  labs(x = "rate, %", y = "$ today per $1 a year for ever")
```

.small[
The paper's text says the lost stream grows, so the rate should be $r - g$, and anchors it at 1.5%
(the S&P 500 dividend yield). The Monte Carlo draws that rate from 1.5% to 4.5%, calls it $r - g$, and
then writes $C/r$. Same numbers, two meanings ([mismatch 3](../materials.html#mismatches)).
Whether the loss lasts **for ever** or about five years is the main objection of the [BSZ report](../../../bsz-analysis/site/) (Boll, Saez
and Zucman).
]

---
name: break-even

# The break-even departure share (Sec 5.3)

$$NPV = 0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x^* = \frac{WT \cdot (r - g)}{C}$$

If less than $x^*$ of the income tax base leaves, the tax pays for itself. Table 10, at the paper's
central revenue, $`r num(n10$WT[1], 0)` billion (= 0.5 × 72), and $C$ = $`r num(n10$C[1], 2)` billion:

```{r t10tab, results="asis"}
cat('<table class="dt"><tr><th></th><th>1.5%</th><th>3.0%</th><th>4.5%</th></tr>')
cat(sprintf("<tr><td>x*</td><td>%s</td></tr>", paste(paste0(num(100 * n10$break_even_pct), "%"), collapse = "</td><td>")))
cat("</table>")
```

.highlight-box[
The draw's central departure share is `r num((nb$f_min + nb$f_max) / 2, 2)`, above $x^*$ at every rate. That is why the
mean NPV comes out negative. Every cell matches the printed Table 10 (PDF p.34).
]

---
name: part-mc
class: center, middle, inverse

# Part 5: The headline

---
name: monte-carlo

# The Monte Carlo behind `r num(h("nber","mc_mean_npv","printed"))` (Sec 5.4)

.pull-left[

Draw 100,000 times, independently:

- revenue $WT \sim U[`r nb$wt_min`, `r nb$wt_max`]$
- income tax $C \sim U[`r nb$c_min`, `r nb$c_max`]$
- rate $(r - g) \sim U[`r nb$rg_min`, `r nb$rg_max`]$
- departure share $f \sim U[`r nb$f_min`, `r nb$f_max`]$

.small[
Revenue is drawn **from zero**: mean `r num(h("nber","mc_expected_revenue"), 0)` = 0.5 × 72. The code never
multiplies by $q$; this zero is its only trace ([mismatch 5](../materials.html#mismatches)). A uniform draw
from 0 has the same **mean** as a coin flip on 72, not the same distribution. Lost income tax is
**not** scaled by $q$: people who left do not come back if the Act is struck down.
]

]

.pull-right[

```{r hist, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=3.2}
ggplot(data.frame(npv = mcn$draws$npv), aes(npv, fill = npv < 0)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, boundary = 0) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(mcn$draws$npv), linetype = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#9a9a9a", `FALSE` = "#555555"), guide = "none") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-250, 70)) + labs(x = "NPV, $B", y = "draws") + theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

]

.blue-box[
The draws are independent, so the mean has a closed form: `r num(tr("npv_mc_nber_analytic_mean"), 2)`.
The printed `r num(h("nber","mc_mean_npv","printed"))` is the authors' seeded run (`r num(mcn$summary$mean, 2)`),
not that expectation. The explorer shows the exact expectation for every setting.
]

---
name: part-argue
class: center, middle, inverse

# Part 6: What to argue about

---
name: seven-inputs

# The seven inputs that move the answer

```{r origins, results="asis"}
cat('<table class="dt"><tr><th>Input</th><th>Values in the explorer</th><th>Origin</th></tr>')
for (d in dials) cat(sprintf("<tr><td>%s</td><td>%s</td><td><span class='og %s'>%s</span></td></tr>",
  d$label, paste(d$labels, collapse = "; "), d$origin, d$origin))
cat("</table>")
```

.highlight-box[
`r sum(vapply(dials, function(d) d$origin == "guesswork", TRUE))` of the `r length(dials)` are guesswork.
The data (Forbes, FTB, the Pareto fit) set the scale; the sign is decided by the guesses.
[Try them in the explorer](../explorer/).
]

name: mismatches

# Mismatches between text, README and code

.small[
```{r mm, results="asis"}
cat(paste0(sub("^([0-9]+)[.] ", "- **Mismatch \\1.** ", mm_lines[!mm_first]), collapse = "\n"))
```
]

.blue-box[
We reproduce the code as shipped and record each discrepancy rather than fix it. Full text on the
[materials page](../materials.html#mismatches); every one is pinned by a test.<sup>1</sup>
]

.footnote[<sup>1</sup> `r c("One","Two","Three","Four","Five","Six","Seven","Eight","Nine")[sum(mm_first)]` more concern only the authors' first version (March 2026): mismatches `r paste(sub("[.].*", "", mm_lines[mm_first]), collapse = ", ")`.]
